blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
When something goes wrong with your laptop, the help desk can only help as fast as your message lets them. A message that says "it doesn't work" starts a ten-minute conversation before anyone can help. A message that says "Outlook crashes every time I open one email from John, it started this morning, and I already restarted twice" gets a real answer in three minutes.

Three simple habits make a big difference. Say exactly what you were doing. Say what happened. And say what you have already tried. Be polite too — the help desk team is busy, and kindness travels fast between colleagues.

Stay available while they work on it, so questions get answered quickly. Good IT support is a two-way conversation. Help the person who is helping you.

items.q: Why can the help desk only help "as fast as your message lets them"?
options: Because your message tells them what the problem is
Because the help desk works very slowly
Because they answer messages in order
Because they need your manager's approval
items.why: "the help desk can only help as fast as your message lets them" — uma boa descrição acelera a ajuda.

items.q: How long does the clear message get an answer in?
items.why: "gets a real answer in three minutes."

items.q: What are the three simple habits in the text?
options: Say what you were doing, what happened, and what you tried
Be fast, be short, and be quiet
items.why: "Say exactly what you were doing… what happened… what you have already tried."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which idea?
options: A clear message helps IT work faster
The message "it doesn't work" is enough to fix the problem
Being polite to the help desk is a good idea
You should stay available while they work
items.why: Inferência: todo o texto mostra que "it doesn't work" é ruim e gera uma conversa longa.

items.q: "Kindness travels fast between colleagues" suggests that…
options: being polite helps you get better help
the help desk is far away
kindness is not important at work
items.why: Inferência: ser gentil com a equipe ocupada faz a relação (e a ajuda) fluir melhor.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Oliver orientando um colega novo. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Hi, come and sit with me for a minute. I saw your message to the help desk this morning. It just said "my email is broken". I know it feels quick, but that message will cost you two hours of waiting.

Let me show you a better way. First, say what you were doing. Second, say what happened. Third, say what you already tried. So we write: "Outlook closes every time I open one email from John. It started this morning. I restarted my laptop twice."

See the difference? Now the help desk knows the problem, the time, and your steps. And please, be polite. Start with "Could you help me, please?" The team is busy, and a kind message really helps.

One more thing. Stay at your desk while they work on it. They may ask a question, and if you answer fast, they fix it fast. Let's send this new message together now.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What was wrong with the new joiner's first message?
options: It only said "my email is broken"
It was sent to the wrong team
items.why: "It just said 'my email is broken'."

items.q: What are the three steps Oliver teaches?
options: Say what you were doing, what happened, and what you tried
Say your name, your team, and your desk
Be short, be fast, and be quiet
items.why: "First, say what you were doing. Second, say what happened. Third, say what you already tried."

items.q: How does Oliver start the polite message?
items.why: "Start with 'Could you help me, please?'"

items.q: Why does Oliver want the new joiner to stay at the desk?
options: To answer the help desk's questions quickly
To restart the computer every hour
items.why: Inferência: "if you answer fast, they fix it fast" — ficar disponível acelera a solução.

items.q: How would you best describe Oliver's tone?
items.why: Inferência: ele senta ao lado, ensina passo a passo e faz junto — é acolhedor.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Please describe the problem in your message." To describe means to…
items.why: To describe = descrever, dizer como a coisa é.

items.q: "My laptop crashes every time I open that file." To crash means to…
items.why: To crash = travar, parar de funcionar de repente.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Please ___ your computer before we look at the problem."
items.why: To restart = reiniciar; é o pedido comum do suporte de TI.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Good IT support is a ___ conversation — both people help each other."
items.why: Two-way = de mão dupla; os dois lados participam.

items.q: "Please stay available while they fix it." Available means…
items.why: Available = disponível, pronto para responder.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em conversas com o suporte de TI. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "IT will look into the problem this afternoon." To look into means to…
items.why: Look into = investigar, examinar o problema.

items.q: "Can you log in again and try?" To log in means to…
options: enter your account with a password
items.why: Log in = entrar na conta com usuário e senha.

items.q: "They will set up the new email for you." To set up means to…
items.why: Set up = configurar, deixar pronto para usar.

items.q: "The help desk will get back to you soon." To get back to someone means to…
items.why: Get back to = retornar, responder depois.

items.q: "Let's sort out this problem together." To sort out means to…
items.why: Sort out = resolver, colocar em ordem.
